title: Cost Sentry: regional instance degradation & preemptible-first fallback plan
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Problem: Tenants are experiencing unexpected bill volatility during regional spot price spikes and spot evictions. Current routing defaults either over-prioritize latency (always prefer on-demand in warm regions) or aggressively use spot which leads to cost overruns and degraded SLOs when eviction cascades occur. We need a lightweight controller (Cost Sentry) that applies tenant-level budget caps and enforces a preemptible-first routing policy with graceful degradation to cheaper model variants and quantized kernels when budget headroom is low.

Goal: Implement a runtime admission and routing layer that evaluates: region price signals, tenant remaining budget for period, accelerator class preference, and model variant compatibility. The layer should decide: prefer spot vs on-demand, select GPU family (A100/V100/GPUx), and when necessary route to a lower-cost model variant (quantized or smaller architecture) with controlled quality degradation. Must support per-tenant soft caps with throttling and hard caps that cause deterministic fallback.

Scope: prototype controller + simulator, integration with router, new routing policy flags, telemetry (per-tenant spend burn-rate, eviction rate, variant-switch count), and a staged rollout behind a feature flag and canary tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Controller accepts spend profile (daily/weekly) and enforces soft/hard caps per tenant.
Router chooses spot resources when price + eviction risk < dynamic threshold and tenant has sufficient headroom.
When budget headroom < soft cap threshold, router will route to compatible cheaper model variant or reduced sequence-length config with a recorded rollback metric.
No customer-facing latency SLOs are violated for P0 tenants during canary (define canary tenants in rollout plan).
Metrics emitted: tenant_spend_remaining, tenant_spend_burn_rate, routing_decision_reason, variant_fallback_count, spot_eviction_count.
E2E smoke test demonstrating degraded variant is accepted by client SDK via deterministic rollout and metric tags.
Demo runbook and rollback instructions present in ticket links.
tasks: Design API for tenant spend profile ingestion and storage (owner: Diego).
Build simulator that replays historical request traces with spot price signals (owner: Rodrigo).
Implement admission controller that returns routing_hint: {prefer_spot, prefer_on_demand, fallback_variant}
Integrate controller into existing smart-router pipeline with feature flag gating (owner: SRE).
Add telemetry + dashboard panels in Console (owner: Observability team).
Run 2-week canary on low-impact tenants and iterate thresholds based on burn-rate signals.
Write SLA/contract tests that ensure for P0 tenants we maintain configured latency SLOs or route to on-demand automatically.
technical_notes: Thresholding: we use a two-tier threshold model: soft_threshold = max(tenant_budget*0.2, fixed_min_usd) and hard_threshold = max(tenant_budget*0.05, fixed_min_usd). Soft threshold triggers graded fallbacks; hard threshold forces strict on-demand block or throttling.

Risk modeling: feed spot eviction probability from cloud telemetry + recent spot reclaim history into a cost-risk score: score = price_ratio * (1 + eviction_prob * eviction_penalty). Router prefers lower score.

Variant compatibility: annotate model catalog with 'fallback_compatibility' tags (quantized-8bit, seq64, small-arch). Router will only select variants that preserve required structured output schemas.
Admission API: POST /admit with {tenant, request_profile} -> returns routing_hint and audit_id. Keep payload small for RT performance (<1ms decision target).
Backpressure: implement per-tenant token bucket tied to spend burn rate to avoid burst overspend during sudden traffic spikes.

Simulation plan: replay 30 days of traffic for 50 tenants with synthetic spot spikes and evaluate cost, latency, and quality regressions. Target improvement: reduce spend volatility by 30% while keeping 95th latency within 10% of baseline for canary tenants.
Data retention: store per-decision audit for 14 days, aggregated metrics for 90 days. Sensitive fields masked in logs.
decisions: Chosen graded fallback instead of binary kill-switch to reduce user surprise and allow for quality-preserving degradations.
Prefer variant substitution (quantized or seq-limited) over routing to a different region when possible to reduce cross-region egress costs and latency penalties.
Use tenant-configurable soft and hard caps with organization defaults. Allow per-route overrides for critical SLAs.
Will not expose raw tenant budget remaining in logs; only emit normalized burn-rate to observability streams for privacy.
Start with deterministic heuristics and metric-based thresholds; plan to ML-optimize selection policy after 2 canaries and sufficient labeled data.
